risks.title: Cyclicality and volatility of oil tanker freight rates
risks.summary: The oil tanker shipping sector is inherently cyclical and volatile. Freight rates depend on external factors (oil supply/demand, regional refining capacity, geopolitical conditions) outside Ardmore's control. A prolonged downturn in rates could render operations unprofitable or generate operating losses.
risks.score_rationale: Risk ranked first in Risk Factor Summary and extensively detailed (paragraphs 1-2 of RISKS RELATED TO OUR INDUSTRY). Intense language: « cyclical and volatile », « prolonged downturn », « unpredictable ». Stable but structural trend. Maximum category weight: directly affects operational profitability.

risks.title: Dependence on geopolitically unstable trade routes
risks.summary: Geopolitical conflicts (Ukraine, Iran-Israel, Hamas-Israel, Houthi attacks in the Red Sea) disrupt major trade routes and oil trading patterns. Ship diversions (Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea) increase voyage expenses and create demand uncertainty. U.S. seizures of tankers near Venezuela add rerouting risks.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned three times in Risk Factor Summary and developed over two full pages (Ukraine conflict, Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea, Venezuela). Highly intense language: « significantly disrupted », « material adverse impact », « unpredictable ». Trend up: new risks (Houthi attacks since December 2023, U.S. seizures in Venezuela). Direct impact on routes, rates, and expenses.

risks.title: Cyberattacks and failures of critical IT systems
risks.summary: Ardmore's IT systems (financial processing, vessel control) are vulnerable to cyberattacks. Threats are increasing in number and sophistication, especially with AI. A breach could disrupt operations, damage reputation, expose the company to litigation, and increase security costs.
risks.score_rationale: Listed third in Risk Factor Summary. Dedicated, detailed paragraph with explicit mention of AI in cyberattacks. Intense language: « vulnerable », « increased in number and sophistication », « significant capital ». Trend up: new mention of AI. Risk specific to vessel control/operations.

risks.title: Counterparty default risk from charterers and commercial partners
risks.summary: Ardmore relies on chartering contracts (spot and time charter) and commercial pool agreements. In depressed market conditions, charterers may refuse to pay or seek cheaper vessels. Default by a major counterparty would reduce revenues and cash flows.
risks.score_rationale: Listed fourth in Risk Factor Summary. Detailed paragraph explaining dependence on chartering contracts and commercial pools. Moderate but clear language: « counterparty risks », « depressed market conditions ». Stable trend. Business-specific risk: charterers' ability to honor contracts.

risks.title: Overcapacity in oil tanker transportation and rate compression
risks.summary: An oversupply of tankers (due to newbuilds, low scrapping, conversions) compresses freight rates and vessel values. Ardmore cannot control overall capacity supply. Prolonged overcapacity reduces profitability and may force loss-making sales.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in Risk Factor Summary (« An over-supply of tanker capacity »). Developed in context of supply (newbuilding deliveries, scrapping rates). Clear language: « reductions in charter rates, vessel values, and profitability ». Stable but structural trend. Direct impact on competitiveness.

risks.title: Operational risks related to vessel damage and off-hire periods
risks.summary: Ardmore's vessels are exposed to operational damage (collisions, storms, wear). Drydocking periods generate unpredictable costs and off-hire downtime. Total losses or repair delays reduce revenues.
risks.score_rationale: Listed in Risk Factor Summary (« damage due to inherent operational risks », « unexpected drydocking costs »). Dedicated paragraph mentioning inherent maritime navigation risks. Moderate language: « may suffer damage », « unexpected costs ». Stable trend. Business-specific risk related to fleet operations.

risks.title: Dependence on a third-party manager and operational continuity risks
risks.summary: Ardmore relies on a third-party manager for the day-to-day operation of its fleet. A failure by the manager (bankruptcy, incompetence, conflicts) could disrupt operations, increase costs, or reduce efficiency. Loss of direct control creates continuity risk.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in Risk Factor Summary (« dependence on our third-party manager »). Risk specific to Ardmore's model (outsourced management). Moderate language. Stable trend. Indirect but significant impact on operational continuity.

risks.title: Shortage of qualified seafarers and rising labor costs
risks.summary: Ardmore must recruit and retain qualified seafarers to crew its vessels. Global maritime crew shortages are increasing wages and complicating recruitment. Inability to secure crews raises operating costs and may reduce vessel availability.
risks.score_rationale: Listed in Risk Factor Summary (« hire or retain qualified seafarers »). Dedicated paragraph highlighting recruitment challenges. Moderate language: « may not be able to hire or retain ». Trend up: structural shortage post-COVID. Direct impact on operating costs.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or AI technologies as a strategic lever. The company references cybersecurity (SIEM and SOC) but does not position AI as a differentiating factor.
evidence: No reference to AI, machine learning, or AI-based automation
Focus on energy efficiency, fleet management, and environmental compliance
Mentioned technological tools (SIEM, SOC) are standard cybersecurity, not AI
